svg.aria-label: Fig 1. The planned Arthai Health flow as nine stations on one bench, every one labeled planned: claim builder, payer mock, remit posting, triage and CCI gate, review console, appeal writer, voice agent, AR follow-up and eval. A green track takes sure claims from the gate to the appeal writer, and a red track takes unsure claims to the human queue. Black tracks carry the claim, the tier-2 approval, the call and the call outcome; a blue dotted track carries reviewer edits to eval and back to the gate.
svg.title: Fig 1. The planned Arthai Health flow as nine stations on one bench, every one labeled planned: claim builder, payer mock, remit posting, triage and CCI gate, review console, appeal writer, voice agent, AR follow-up and eval. A green track takes sure claims from the gate to the appeal writer, and a red track takes unsure claims to the human queue. Black tracks carry the claim, the tier-2 approval, the call and the call outcome; a blue dotted track carries reviewer edits to eval and back to the gate.
svg.text: Synthetic data only. Every station is planned. None is built yet.
1 Claim builder and scrubber: builds the 837 claim file and runs the NCCI and MUE edits.
2 Payer and clearinghouse mock: our own fake payer. It sends 835 and 277 files.
3 Remit posting: reads the 835 remittance and finds each denied line.
4 Triage + CCI gate: the scorer (LLM by default, LAYA optional) and a conformal set pick the path.
5 Review console + audit: the human queue, the approvals and the audit trail.
6 Appeal writer: Muse drafts the letter. Each statement cites a source.
7 Voice agent: a browser call to the mock payer rep.
8 AR follow-up: ranks the open claims for the next action.
9 Eval and feedback loop: reviewer edits become eval cases.
green: the gate is sure, 4 to 6.
red: the gate is not sure, 4 to the human queue in 5. After the human decides, 5 to 6.
black: the claim moves 1 to 2 to 3 to 4. The draft goes 6 to 5 for tier-2 approval.
black: after approval, 5 to 7 (send, then call). The call outcome goes 7 to 8.
dashed: the call goes only to our mock payer in 2.
blue dotted: reviewer edits go 5 to 9, then recalibrate the gate in 4.
